questions.question: The 9th Asian Games was hosted by which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **9th Asian Games** were hosted by **India** in the year **1982**.
 
• This event marked the **first time India hosted the Asian Games** since the inaugural edition in 1951.
 
• The games took place in **New Delhi**, the capital city of India.
 
• A total of **4,595 athletes** from **33 nations** participated in the event.
 
• The mascot of the 1982 Asian Games was **Appu**, an elephant, symbolizing **strength and prosperity.**
 
• The event featured **21 sports disciplines**, including athletics, hockey, swimming, and football.
 
• The 9th Asian Games in 1982 were significant for introducing advanced technologies such as **color television broadcasting** in India.
 
• India performed impressively, winning a total of **57 medals**, including **13 gold medals.**
 
• The games were organized under the supervision of the **Indian Olympic Association**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **China**__

 __
 
• **China** has hosted the Asian Games multiple times, including the **11th Asian Games in 1990** in Beijing.
 
• China is known for its **dominance in sports** at the Asian Games, often topping the medal tally.
 
 
 
• **South Korea**__
 __
 
• **South Korea** hosted the Asian Games for the first time in **1986**, the **10th edition**, held in Seoul.
 
• South Korea is also known for hosting the **2002 Asian Games** in Busan.
 
 
 
• **Japan**__
 
 
• **Japan** hosted the Asian Games twice: in **1958 (3rd edition)** and **2014 (17th edition)**.
 
• Japan is recognized for its contributions to the development of **modern sports infrastructure** in Asia.

questions.question: A child is a picky eater. He does not consume milk at all and barely eats other kinds of food. When he started losing his baby teeth, they were not getting replaced with new teeth. This can be solved by giving him _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**calcium supplements**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Calcium is an essential **mineral** required for the development and maintenance of **strong bones and teeth**.
 
• In children, a lack of calcium can lead to **poor dental health**, including delayed eruption of new teeth.
 
• Calcium plays a crucial role in the process of **tooth formation** (odontogenesis) by strengthening the teeth's enamel and dentin.
 
• Milk and dairy products are primary sources of calcium, but for a child who is a **picky eater** and avoids milk, **calcium supplements** can serve as an alternative.
 
• Calcium deficiency in children can also lead to **weakened bones**, increasing the risk of conditions such as rickets.
 
• Providing calcium supplements, along with a balanced diet, ensures that the child gets the recommended daily intake of calcium for healthy growth.
 
• Other dietary sources of calcium include **leafy green vegetables, fortified cereals, tofu, and nuts.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vitamin B Complex**__

 __
 
• **Vitamin B complex** includes a group of water-soluble vitamins that play a role in **metabolism, energy production, and red blood cell formation.**
 
• A deficiency of vitamin B may lead to **fatigue, anemia, or nerve issues**, but it is not directly linked to tooth development.
 
 
 
• **Carbohydrate-rich Food**__
 __
 
• **Carbohydrates** are the primary source of **energy** for the body.
 
• While they are important for overall health, they do not contribute to **tooth development** or the replacement of teeth.
 
 
 
• **Vitamin C**__
 
 
• **Vitamin C** is vital for the **repair and growth of tissues** and supports the immune system.
 
• A deficiency of vitamin C can lead to conditions like **scurvy**, but it does not directly impact tooth formation or calcium absorption.

questions.question: Kala Ramnath belonged to which of the following gharanas?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Mewati gharana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kala Ramnath** is an internationally acclaimed Indian classical violinist known for her innovative style.
 
• She belongs to the **Mewati Gharana**, a school of Indian classical music with a rich heritage.
 
• The **Mewati Gharana** is particularly noted for its emphasis on **bhakti (devotional expression)** and lyrical quality in music.
 
• It was established by **Pt. Natthan Khan** and gained prominence through musicians like **Pt. Jasraj**.
 
• Kala Ramnath has been trained under the guidance of **Pt. Jasraj**, one of the most renowned exponents of the Mewati Gharana.
 
• Her musical style incorporates traditional Indian classical music along with elements that appeal to a global audience.
 
• Kala Ramnath has performed across the world and collaborated with several international artists, showcasing the versatility of Indian classical music.
 
• She has received numerous accolades and awards for her contribution to music, including recognition as one of the finest violinists in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Agra Gharana**__

 __
 
• The **Agra Gharana** is one of the oldest and most prominent schools of Hindustani classical music.
 
• It is known for its emphasis on **dhrupad and khayal styles** of singing.
 
• Established by **Haji Sujan Khan**, it gained fame through singers like **Faiyaz Khan**.
 
 
 
• **Kirana Gharana**__
 __
 
• The **Kirana Gharana** focuses on perfecting **tonal quality** and emphasizes melody over rhythm.
 
• It was founded by **Abdul Karim Khan** and has produced legendary musicians like **Bhimsen Joshi**.
 
 
 
• **Indore Gharana**__
 
 
• The **Indore Gharana** is known for its unique approach to khayal singing.
 
• It was popularized by **Ustad Amir Khan**, who emphasized slow, meditative renditions.
 
• The gharana is celebrated for its intellectual depth and innovative style.

questions.question: Anuradhapura, the old capital of Sri Lanka, was destroyed by which of the following dynasties of South India in the 10th century AD?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Chola**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chola dynasty** was one of the longest-ruling dynasties in South Indian history, noted for its contributions to art, architecture, administration, and military power.
 
• In the **10th century AD**, the Chola rulers expanded their empire significantly, conquering territories across South India and Sri Lanka.
 
• Under the reign of **Raja Raja Chola I** and his successors, the Chola Empire reached its zenith, demonstrating remarkable administrative skills and military prowess.
 
• The Cholas invaded Sri Lanka, destroyed its capital city, **Anuradhapura**, and established their dominance over the region.
 
• They replaced the capital with another city, **Polonnaruwa**, marking a significant shift in Sri Lankan history.
 
• The Chola rulers were known for their maritime ambitions, which enabled them to maintain trade links and exercise control over territories beyond the Indian mainland.
 
• The invasion of Anuradhapura highlighted the Chola dynasty's strategic military planning and imperial ambition in South Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rashtrakuta**__

 __
 
• The **Rashtrakuta dynasty** was a prominent South Indian dynasty known for its contributions to art, culture, and architecture.
 
• They were patrons of art and are credited with building the famous **Kailasa Temple** at Ellora.
 
• However, they were not involved in the destruction of **Anuradhapura**.
 
 
 
• **Chalukyas of Badami**__
 __
 
• The **Chalukyas of Badami** ruled parts of South India between the 6th and 8th centuries AD and were known for their architectural achievements, such as the **Aihole and Pattadakal temples**.
 
• They did not participate in the invasion or destruction of Anuradhapura.
 
 
 
• **Chalukyas of Vengi**__
 
 
• The **Chalukyas of Vengi** were a branch of the Chalukya dynasty, ruling parts of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
 
• They were primarily focused on regional dominance and were not involved in the destruction of Sri Lankan capitals.

questions.question: Which writ is issued by the High Court or Supreme Court when a lower court considers a case going beyond its jurisdiction?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Prohibition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The writ of **Prohibition** is issued by a higher court (High Court or Supreme Court) to a lower court or tribunal to **prevent it from exceeding its jurisdiction** or acting outside its legal authority.
 
• It is issued when the lower court or tribunal is found to be acting **without or beyond its jurisdiction** in a particular case.
 
• The purpose of the writ is to **stop judicial overreach** or illegal proceedings before a final decision is made.
 
• This writ is a **preventive measure**, ensuring that the lower court or tribunal does not commit an error of jurisdiction.
 
• It is important to note that **Prohibition** is issued only when the proceedings are ongoing and not after the decision has been made.
 
• Prohibition is a **constitutional remedy** provided under Articles **32** and **226** of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mandamus**__

 __
 
• **Mandamus** is a writ issued by a court to a public official, asking them to perform their **statutory duties** which they have failed to do.
 
• It is a **command** issued to ensure that public officials or bodies act according to the law.
 
• The term **Mandamus** means "We Command" in Latin.
 
 
 
• **Habeas Corpus**__
 __
 
• The writ of **Habeas Corpus**, meaning "You may have the body" in Latin, is issued to ensure that a person who is detained is brought before the court to examine whether the detention is **lawful**.
 
• It is a safeguard for the **personal liberty** of individuals against unlawful detention.
 
 
 
• **Quo Warranto**__
 
 
• The writ of **Quo Warranto** is issued to inquire into the **legality of a person's claim** to a public office.
 
• It prevents an individual from holding a public office they are **not entitled** to.

questions.question: Every year, Karthik Purnima marks the end of a livestock fair in Pushkar, where the main animal on display is:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**camel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The annual **Pushkar Fair**, also known as the **Karthik Purnima Fair**, is one of the largest livestock fairs in India.
 
• The **camel** is the main animal displayed, bought, and sold at the fair. It is often referred to as the **"Ship of the Desert"** and holds significant economic and cultural importance in the region.
 
• The fair is held in **Pushkar**, a town in the Ajmer district of **Rajasthan**, and is particularly famous for its **camel trading and camel races.**
 
• The Pushkar Fair coincides with the holy day of **Karthik Purnima**, attracting devotees for religious rituals and tourists for cultural festivities.
 
• The event is also a hub for showcasing traditional **Rajasthani culture**, including folk music, dance, and crafts.
 
• The camel, being a crucial part of **Rajasthan's desert ecosystem**, is celebrated and showcased prominently during the fair.
 
• The fair contributes to the local economy through tourism and livestock trade, with camels being a central aspect of the event.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cow**__

 __
 
• The **cow** holds a sacred place in Indian culture and is associated with religious and agricultural significance.
 
• It is not the primary animal displayed at the Pushkar Fair, as the focus is on camels and other livestock.
 
 
 
• **Horse**__
 __
 
• The **horse** is also traded at the Pushkar Fair but is not as prominent as the camel.
 
• Horses are valued for their use in agriculture and ceremonial purposes, particularly in Rajasthan.
 
 
 
• **Buffalo**__
 
 
• **Buffaloes** are commonly associated with milk production and agricultural work.
 
• While they are traded in livestock fairs, they are not the main focus of the Pushkar Fair.

questions.question: Which of the following organisations in India provides facilities for acquisition of satellite data and its processing?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC)** is a key organization under the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** that provides facilities for the acquisition and processing of satellite data.
 
• It is located in **Hyderabad, Telangana**, and operates through regional centers across India.
 
• The NRSC is responsible for acquiring data from various **Earth Observation (EO) satellites** launched by ISRO as well as other international space agencies.
 
• It plays a crucial role in **remote sensing applications**, which include **agriculture, forestry, water resources, urban planning, disaster management, and environmental monitoring**.
 
• NRSC provides processed data in the form of **satellite images** and **geospatial information** for use by researchers, government agencies, and private organizations.
 
• It also maintains and operates **ground stations** to receive real-time satellite data.
 
• The processed data is used for creating **GIS (Geographic Information System) tools**, which are essential for effective decision-making in various domains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Forest Research Institute (FRI)**__

 __
 
• The **Forest Research Institute (FRI)** is located in **Dehradun, Uttarakhand**.
 
• It focuses on **forestry research** and education, particularly in areas like forest ecology, biodiversity, and sustainable forestry practices.
 
• The FRI does not deal with satellite data acquisition or processing.
 
 
 
• **Indian Institute of Remote Sensing (IIRS)**__
 __
 
• The **Indian Institute of Remote Sensing (IIRS)** is a premier institute under **ISRO**, based in **Dehradun, Uttarakhand**.
 
• It provides **training and education** in remote sensing, geoinformatics, and GIS applications.
 
• While IIRS supports training and capacity building, it does not directly handle satellite data acquisition and processing, which is the domain of NRSC.
 
 
 
• **Wildlife Institute of India (WII)**__
 
 
• The **Wildlife Institute of India (WII)** is located in **Dehradun, Uttarakhand**.
 
• It focuses on **wildlife research, conservation, and management**.
 
• The WII does not deal with satellite data processing but may use such data for wildlife habitat studies.

questions.question: Which of the following is included in the estimation of Gross National Product?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Sale of new shirts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gross National Product (GNP)** is the total market value of all final goods and services produced by a country's residents in a given time period, regardless of where the production takes place.
 
• The **sale of new shirts** is included in GNP because it represents the production of a **final good** within the economy.
 
• GNP includes the value of **newly produced goods and services**, which are counted at their market value to avoid double counting.
 
• The production of new goods like shirts contributes to the **economic output** and reflects the labor, capital, and other inputs used in manufacturing.
 
• It excludes intermediate goods to prevent **double-counting**, which ensures that only the value of final goods is included.
 
• This type of transaction adds to the overall economic activity and is measured as part of the GNP of a country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pension payments**__

 __
 
• Pension payments are **transfer payments**, meaning they are not made in exchange for goods or services. Hence, they are not included in the GNP.
 
• Transfer payments do not reflect current production or economic activity but are rather a redistribution of income.
 
 
 
• **Sale of securities**__
 __
 
• The sale of securities (like stocks and bonds) is considered a financial transaction and does not represent the production of goods or services.
 
• Such transactions are excluded from GNP as they do not contribute to the economic output.
 
 
 
• **Sale of used cars**__
 
 
• The sale of used cars is not included in GNP because it does not represent the production of new goods or services.
 
• Only the value of new production is counted in GNP to avoid double-counting the value of goods produced in previous years.

questions.question: When was the Jallianwala Bagh massacre brought into action by the Britishers in Amritsar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 13 April, 1919.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Jallianwala Bagh massacre** occurred on **April 13, 1919**, in **Amritsar, Punjab**, when British troops under the command of **General Dyer** opened fire on a large crowd of unarmed civilians.
 
• The crowd had gathered to protest against the repressive **Rowlatt Act** imposed by the British government, which allowed arrests without trial, further fueling anger among the Indian population.
 
• The massacre resulted in the deaths of hundreds of people, with estimates varying between **379 to 1,000**, and thousands more wounded. The incident sparked widespread outrage across India and was a turning point in the Indian independence movement.
 
• The event became a symbol of British brutality and ignited mass protests and a more determined resistance against colonial rule. It was one of the major catalysts for the **Non-Cooperation Movement** led by **Mahatma Gandhi**.

questions.question: In January 2023, the Chief Minister's Residential Land Rights Scheme (Mukhyamantri Awasiya Bhu Adhikar Yojana) was launched in which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chief Minister's Residential Land Rights Scheme**, also known as the **Mukhyamantri Awasiya Bhu Adhikar Yojana**, was launched in January 2023 in the Indian state of **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• This scheme aims to provide **residential land rights** to families that do not own land for constructing houses.
 
• The initiative is particularly focused on benefitting the **economically weaker sections** of society and ensuring that they have access to secure housing.
 
• Under this scheme, eligible families are provided with **free land plots of 600 square feet** to construct their homes.
 
• The scheme is a part of the state's efforts to achieve the broader goal of **housing for all**, aligning with the vision of the **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana** at the national level.
 
• The scheme also aims to bring social and economic upliftment by ensuring that people have access to basic amenities and a stable place to live.
 
• The Madhya Pradesh government has been actively working to provide **land and housing security** to its citizens, especially in rural areas, through this initiative.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Haryana**__

 __
 
• **Haryana** is located in northern India and is known for its significant contributions to **agriculture** and **industrial development**.
 
• The state is famous for the **Green Revolution** and is a major producer of crops like wheat and rice.
 
• It has also introduced several welfare schemes, but the **Mukhyamantri Awasiya Bhu Adhikar Yojana** is not one of them.
 
 
 
• **Punjab**__
 __
 
• **Punjab**, another northern Indian state, is renowned for its **rich cultural heritage** and being the **breadbasket of India**.
 
• Punjab has implemented various housing and welfare programs but is not associated with the **Chief Minister's Residential Land Rights Scheme**.
 
 
 
• **Uttar Pradesh**__
 
 
• **Uttar Pradesh** is the most populous state in India, known for its **historic landmarks** and **agricultural economy**.
 
• The state government has implemented multiple housing schemes such as **PMAY-Gramin**, but the **Mukhyamantri Awasiya Bhu Adhikar Yojana** pertains specifically to Madhya Pradesh.

questions.question: The Citadel area has a huge mud _______ platform, which is 6 m high and underlies all the construction.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**brick**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Citadel area** mentioned in the question refers to the elevated and fortified portions of settlements in the **Indus Valley Civilization**.
 
• The platform underneath the Citadel was made of **mud bricks**, which were a primary construction material used during the **Harappan period**.
 
• **Bricks** were crucial to the architecture of the Indus Valley Civilization, and they were generally **rectangular in shape** and standardized in size.
 
• The use of **mud bricks** in the platform ensured stability and served as a strong foundation for the construction of important structures like **granaries, public baths, and administrative buildings**.
 
• Harappan bricks were made by combining **clay, sand, and water**, which were then sun-dried or baked in kilns to harden them, ensuring durability.
 
• These bricks were laid in an **interlocking pattern** to provide strength to the platform and make it resistant to natural calamities like earthquakes.
 
• The elevated mud brick platform also served to protect structures from **floods**, which were common in the region due to the proximity of rivers like the **Indus**.
 
• The use of mud bricks reflects the **advanced urban planning** and engineering skills of the Harappan people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Stone**__

 __
 
• **Stone** was not the primary material used in the Indus Valley Civilization for constructing platforms or buildings, as the region lacked abundant stone resources.
 
• However, stone was used for making **tools, seals, weights, and ornaments**.
 
 
 
• **Rock**__
 __
 
• **Rock** structures are more commonly associated with later historical periods, such as the **Mauryan Empire**, where rock-cut architecture became prominent.
 
• The Indus Valley sites primarily relied on mud bricks rather than carved rock structures.
 
 
 
• **Wood**__
 
 
• **Wood** was used in the Indus Valley Civilization for making doors, window frames, and smaller structures but not for constructing platforms.
 
• Wooden artifacts, including carts and furniture, have been discovered in excavations.

questions.question: Who is the author of the English novel 'Voting at Fosterganj'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ruskin Bond**__.

questions.question: The Indus Water Treaty took place in _______ between India and Pakistan.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**1960**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Indus Water Treaty** was signed in the year **1960** between India and Pakistan.
 
• This treaty was mediated by the **World Bank** to resolve disputes regarding the use of water from the **Indus River system**.
 
• The treaty divided the rivers of the Indus basin between the two countries: **India received the eastern rivers** (Sutlej, Beas, and Ravi) while **Pakistan received the western rivers** (Indus, Jhelum, and Chenab).
 
• It is considered one of the most successful examples of water-sharing agreements between two nations and has survived multiple conflicts and wars.
 
• The Indus Water Treaty outlines mechanisms for cooperation, data sharing, and dispute resolution through a **Permanent Indus Commission** comprising representatives from both countries.
 
• The treaty ensures that the flows of the **western rivers** are not obstructed by India, while Pakistan has no claim over the **eastern rivers.**
 
• This treaty is significant for maintaining **peaceful relations** between the two countries despite their historical and ongoing tensions.

questions.question: What is the atomic number of uranium (U)?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**92**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uranium** is a chemical element with the symbol **U** and atomic number **92**.
 
• It is a **radioactive element** that belongs to the actinide series in the periodic table.
 
• Uranium is used primarily as **fuel in nuclear reactors** and to produce **nuclear weapons**.
 
• It is found naturally in **earth's crust**, primarily as uranium-238 and uranium-235 isotopes.
 
• Uranium-235 is significant because of its ability to undergo **nuclear fission**, which is used in nuclear power generation.
 
• Uranium is mined in various countries, including **Canada, Kazakhstan, and Australia**.
 
• It is processed into **yellowcake**, a concentrated form of uranium oxide, before being used in reactors.
 
• The discovery of Uranium dates back to **1789** by German chemist Martin Heinrich Klaproth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Rutherfordium**:**__

 __
 
• Atomic number **104** corresponds to the element **Rutherfordium**, not Uranium.
 
• Rutherfordium is a **synthetic element** and is part of the transition metals group.
 
• It was first discovered in **1964** by a team of Russian scientists.
 
 
 
• Plutonium**:**__
 __
 
• Atomic number **94** corresponds to the element **Plutonium**.
 
• Plutonium is a **radioactive actinide metal** and is used in **nuclear reactors** and **nuclear weapons**.
 
• It was first isolated in **1940** by scientists at the University of California, Berkeley.
 
 
 
• Thorium**:**__
 
 
• Atomic number **90** corresponds to the element **Thorium**.
 
• Thorium is a **weakly radioactive metal** and is considered a potential alternative to uranium in **nuclear reactors.**
 
• It was discovered in **1828** by Swedish chemist Jöns Jakob Berzelius.

questions.question: Tsunami is a natural disaster that originates from the ocean. The cause of Tsunami in the ocean is:

options.text: The movement of tectonic plates under the ocean
The alarmingly increasing amount of acid in water
The presence of excessive carbon dioxide in the water
The accumulation of high amount of radioactive pollutants in the ocean

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**The movement of tectonic plates under the ocean**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **tsunami** is a series of large waves caused by the sudden displacement of water in the ocean, typically due to geological activities.
 
• The primary cause of tsunamis is the **movement of tectonic plates**, particularly underwater earthquakes along **subduction zones**.
 
• Subduction zones occur where one tectonic plate slides beneath another, leading to immense pressure and potential for sudden release during an earthquake.
 
• Other geological events such as **underwater volcanic eruptions**, **landslides**, or **meteorite impacts** can also trigger tsunamis, but earthquakes are the most common cause.
 
• The movement of tectonic plates creates seismic activity that can displace large volumes of water, generating waves that travel across the ocean at high speeds.
 
• These waves can grow in height as they approach shallow coastal areas, causing catastrophic destruction upon impact.
 
• Tsunamis are different from regular ocean waves as they involve the movement of the entire water column, not just the surface.
 
• The term "tsunami" originates from the Japanese words **"tsu" (harbor)** and **"nami" (wave)**.
 
• Monitoring and early warning systems for tsunamis rely on detecting seismic activity and changes in ocean levels using equipment like **seismometers** and **buoys**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The alarmingly increasing amount of acid in water**__

 __
 
• While excessive acidity in oceans, caused by **ocean acidification**, is a result of increased absorption of **carbon dioxide (CO₂)**, it does not cause tsunamis.
 
• Ocean acidification impacts marine life and ecosystems but does not trigger large-scale wave movements.
 
 
 
• **The presence of excessive carbon dioxide in the water**__
 __
 
• **Excessive carbon dioxide** in oceans primarily contributes to ocean acidification and climate change.
 
• This phenomenon affects marine organisms like coral reefs but is unrelated to the geological causes of tsunamis.
 
 
 
• **The accumulation of high amount of radioactive pollutants in the ocean**__
 
 
• Radioactive pollution in oceans typically arises from **nuclear accidents** or improper disposal of waste.
 
• Though it poses severe environmental risks, it does not generate the physical forces required to create tsunamis.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement regarding Ozone.

options.text: Ozone is formed from oxygen in the presence of ultraviolet radiation.
Ozone (O₃), like oxygen, is a life-supporting gas.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Ozone (O3), like oxygen, is a life-supporting gas.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ozone (O3)** is a triatomic molecule composed of three oxygen atoms.
 
• Unlike oxygen gas (O2), ozone is highly reactive and does not support life as oxygen does.
 
• **Ozone** is primarily found in the **stratosphere**, where it forms the ozone layer, protecting living organisms from harmful **ultraviolet radiation (UV).**
 
• While ozone in the stratosphere plays a protective role, ozone at ground level is considered a harmful air pollutant and can cause respiratory issues.
 
• **Ozone** is toxic and a deadly poison to living organisms when inhaled in significant amounts.
 
• Its primary formation mechanism involves the interaction between oxygen molecules and **UV radiation** from the sun.
 
• Thus, ozone cannot be classified as a life-supporting gas like oxygen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ozone is formed from oxygen in the presence of ultraviolet radiation.**__

 __
 
• **Ozone formation** occurs when ultraviolet radiation splits oxygen molecules (O2) into oxygen atoms, which then combine with other oxygen molecules to form ozone (O3).
 
• This process predominantly occurs in the **stratosphere**, leading to the formation of the ozone layer.
 
 
 
• **Ultraviolet radiation causes skin cancer.**__
 __
 
• **UV radiation** is a known carcinogen that can damage DNA in skin cells, leading to conditions such as **melanoma** and other types of skin cancer.
 
• The ozone layer absorbs a significant portion of harmful UV radiation, reducing the risk of skin cancer for living organisms.
 
 
 
• **Ozone is a deadly poison.**__
 
 
• **Ozone** is toxic to humans and animals when inhaled in high concentrations.
 
• Exposure to ozone can cause respiratory problems, inflammation of the lungs, and other health issues.
 
• It is classified as an air pollutant at ground level.
